name: Shaphat
overview: Shaphat was a male servant in the time of King David, entrusted with the responsibility of overseeing the king's cattle in the valleys. His role highlights a position of trust and management within David's administration. No tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaphat means 'he judges.' This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:29, does not appear to have been given directly by God but reflects a common Hebrew name with judicial connotations.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Shaphat as the son of Adlai, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Shaphat's significance lies in his trusted role within King David's household, specifically managing the king's cattle, which would have been a valuable asset. His mention in the biblical text underscores the organized and delegated nature of David's administration. While not a prominent figure in theological narratives, Shaphat exemplifies faithful service in the practical affairs of the kingdom.
